newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares drop following bomb attack.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares drop following bomb attack.

text.p: Tel Aviv shares on Wednesday afternoon reversed morning gains after two bombs ripped through an outdoor market in Jewish west Jerusalem, killing at least 18 people, traders said.
In afternoon trading the Mishtanim index of top 100 shares was down 1.1 percent or 3.42 points at 302.13 while the Maof 25 blue chip index was down 1.4 percent at 309.15.
In the morning the Maof had risen by as much as 0.73 percent.
"Right after we heard about the attack and about the size of the attack people began selling," said Ilan Doron of Solid Financial Markets.
"I don't think, though, that this marks a change in trend. This was a spontaneous reaction to an event like this."
Doron said that in the past the market has usually fallen in the first day or two following such an attack but then completely recovers.
"In the long term such attacks don't affect the market," Doron said.
He said he expected the market to continue its upward path.
Shortly after the bombs exploded the shekel also began weakening, falling to 3.55 shekels to the dollar from 3.53 in the morning.
A Bank Hapoalim dealer said he did not believe the weakness was tied to the attack.
